rationale: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=FRESH search-20260619-01 iter-1 FEASIBILITY (corrected protocol: val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV; HARD 20-min train+score budget; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-step model.projector swap, bg_target=truth, no fov= override). Hammernik-VN = MRI variational net ported to CT: T untied unrolled steps, each = learned filter-bank + per-filter RBF activation (the _rho_prime bump loop) PLUS an in-loop PYRO-NN projector data-consistency step (architectural twin of LPD/ItNet but tiny interpretable regulariser). CRITICAL LESSON from the SIBLING hammernik_2017 iter-1: it did NOT diverge to 0.0 -- it CUDA-OOM'd in _rho_prime at 72s with batch_size=4 (16GB RTX5000; the (B,F,H,W)=(4,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF tensors + 5-step autograd blew the card). So the dominant iter-1 risk here is MEMORY, not divergence. MITIGATION: batch_size=2 (NOT 4), vn_n_filters=16 (below the 24 default -> fewer RBF tensors), vn_checkpoint=true (gradient-checkpoints each unrolled step -- hammernik_vn HAS this knob, cuts activation memory ~T-fold; this is the key difference that lets the projector-in-loop VN fit where the 2017 batch=4 did not). STABILITY against the documented VN family divergence/NaN->0.0 trap: grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY -- the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward; clip_and_step also SKIPS nonfinite-gradient batches so a poisoned step can't collapse the recon to a constant), vn_dc_norm=true (power-iter normalizes R^T(Rx-g) so softplus(lambda_t) stays O(1) regardless of geometry -- the safeguard the projector-less 2017 lacked), lr=5e-4 (the documented hammernik_vn optimum from the discarded run; 8e-4 was worse, brief caps lr<=5e-4), vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3 (loose VN-port working-corner hint). CAPACITY conservative per brief: vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0 (FBP recon is ~O(1) so the RBF grid [-1,1] covers it). BUDGET: reference -- LPD (projector-in-loop, T=7, ep30, train200, score214) ran 1150s/19.2min right at the edge; hammernik_vn at T=5/N_k=16/checkpointed should be comparable-or-cheaper per step. max_train_s=1000 (16.7min in-solver wall) is the BINDING constraint (epochs=14 is just an upper bound the wall trips first), leaving ~3min for score(214)+figure under the 30min SLURM kill. HYPOTHESIS: if I run a budget-sized, MEMORY-SAFE (batch=2, checkpointed), STABLE (grad_clip=1.0, dc_norm) Hammernik-VN, I expect (a) it AVOIDS the hammernik_2017 OOM and produces a FINITE val_ssim within 20min, and (b) the projector DC step lands it near or above the ~0.84 LD-FBP SSIM floor -- because a learned-regulariser + true-projector-DC unroll is a sound Mayo recon family (sibling LPD/ItNet/DD-sup all run finite here). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric VN baseline that iter-2+ tunes one knob at a time (epochs/wall first to confirm convergence, then vn_T or vn_lambda_init).

BUDGET: 24 filters ~1.3x the per-step RBF/conv cost; iter-1 did 7 ep in 1000s (143 s/ep) so expect ~5 ep in the 1000s wall -- still >3 (convergence point), so the converged-comparison is fair. Memory safe: vn_checkpoint=true + batch_size=2 keep N_k=24 (the solver memory-fitted default) within the card. max_train_s=1000 unchanged; total ~1300s under the 1800s SLURM kill.

column13: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.05, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=10, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_vn iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: vn_lambda_init 0.0023 -> 0.05 (~22x DC-weight init). All else held at iter-2 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_init=fbp, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). PRIOR (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (vn_n_filters=16, hr=0, elapsed 1295.7s); iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (vn_n_filters=24, hr=0, elapsed 1351.7s, train 1191.6s). The iter-2 filter bump 16->24 did NOT help -- it REGRESSED -0.0133 (0.80528->0.79195). Both sit BELOW the LD-FBP floor (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR=34.08), so hr=0. This FIRES iter-2's own pre-registered falsifier ('if val_ssim stays <=0.81 still <FBP, the VN is smoothing-bound regardless of filter count, iter-3 must raise the DC weight vn_lambda_init'). DIAGNOSIS from iter-2 SLURM log 765279: dc_norm power-iter ~= 1.47e+03; training CONVERGED (loss 4.9e-4 ep1 -> 1.3e-6 ep6, flat by ep3) -- NOT under-training, so epochs-up is INERT; and CRITICALLY lambda_t stayed pinned at ['0.0023','0.00231','0.00231','0.00231','0.00231'] across ALL epochs -- Adam never grew the learnable DC weight from its init. The update is u <- u - KT_rho - lam * R^T(Ru-g)/dc_norm (solver lines 141-156): with lam ~= 0.0023 the data-consistency pull is negligible vs the learned regulariser gradient KT_rho, so the VN converges to a blunt smoother that degrades the FBP init below baseline. LIMITER = DC weight too small (NOT capacity: filters^ regressed; NOT epochs: loss flat). Since lambda_t never moves from init, the init vn_lambda_init IS the lever. vn_lambda_init 0.0023 -> 0.05 makes data-consistency dominate the regulariser from step 1 so the recon stays anchored to the measured sinogram instead of over-smoothing. lr held (campaign has lr5e-4-optimal / 8e-4-worse on record). HYPOTHESIS: with the DC init ~22x stronger, val_ssim clears the FBP floor (val_ssim > 0.84, hr>0). FALSIFIER: if val_ssim stays <=0.84 (still <FBP), the VN regulariser is structurally degrading even under strong DC, and iter-4 must attack the regulariser itself (vn_normalize_filters=True to constrain filters zero-mean/unit-norm, or vn_init=backproj). BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): the lambda VALUE does not change per-step compute (same forward/back-project DC step), so cost ~= iter-2: train 1191.6s (max_train_s=1000 binds, ~6 epochs) + ~160s score(214)+figure = ~1352s, under the 1800s SLURM kill. MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-2 -- batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=24 within the 16 GB card (no OOM; cf. the hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise -- and a stronger DC step makes the clip MORE load-bearing).

hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.05, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=True, epochs=10, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_vn iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). LAST-LEVER / confirmation iter. ONE KNOB on the REGULARIZER (not capacity, not lambda): vn_normalize_filters False -> True (constrain each learned filter K_i to zero-mean + unit-norm, the paper-faithful constraint, solver _effective_weight lines 119-128). All else held at iter-3 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_lambda_init=0.05, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_init=fbp, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, all BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (vn_n_filters=16, elapsed 1295.7s); iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (vn_n_filters=24, capacity UP -> REGRESSED -0.0133, elapsed 1351.7s); iter-3 SSIM 0.768197 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05, DC-weight ~22x UP -> REGRESSED -0.0238, elapsed 1159.6s, val_psnr 32.07, val_rmse 1.246e-3). BOTH structural levers already attacked the wrong thing: capacity-UP regressed AND DC-weight-UP regressed, so the recon sits monotonically BELOW its own FBP init (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR 34.08). FAILURE MODE (well-characterized): the learned VN regulariser term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i u) is a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init below baseline, and it does so REGARDLESS of capacity (filters^ hurt) or DC weight (lambda^ hurt). This FIRES iter-3's own pre-registered falsifier: 'if SSIM stays <=0.84 under strong DC, the VN regulariser is structurally degrading -> iter-4 attacks the regulariser itself: vn_normalize_filters=True OR vn_init=backproj'. CHOICE OF KNOB (most diagnostic remaining): vn_normalize_filters=True is the SHARPEST test of the smoothing diagnosis, and is preferred over vn_init=backproj (which changes only the init, not the regularizer mechanism, and the baseline is pinned to FBP either way). MECHANISM: zero-mean filters have NO DC response -- conv with a zero-mean kernel annihilates any uniform/low-frequency level component -- so a zero-mean-unit-norm-constrained K_i CANNOT apply a uniform smoothing or level shift to the image; the regulariser term can only act on local CONTRAST (edges/texture). Unit-norm caps each filter's gain so no single filter can dominate and over-smooth. If the iter-1/2/3 degradation was the unconstrained filters collapsing to a DC/low-pass smoother, this constraint removes that failure path -> the recon should stop sinking below the FBP init and hr should rise toward / above 0. HYPOTHESIS: with zero-mean unit-norm filters the regulariser stops smoothing the FBP init below baseline; val_ssim clears the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr > 0). FALSIFIER (the terminal one): if val_ssim still <= 0.84 (below FBP) with the regulariser CONSTRAINED, then hammernik_vn is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED on rebinned Mayo regardless of regulariser config (capacity, DC weight, AND filter constraint all exhausted) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT: the Hammernik-VN learned-regulariser family does not beat LD-FBP on real 2304-view Mayo LDCT, and drive the remaining iters to document the ceiling, not chase it. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): the zero-mean/unit-norm normalization is a cheap per-step reshape (filter tensor is (24,1,11,11)); per-step forward/back-project DC cost is IDENTICAL to iter-3, so wall ~= iter-3 (1159.6s) -- well under the 1800s SLURM kill, ~640s margin. MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-3 -- batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=24 within the 16 GB RTX5000 (no OOM; cf. the hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM at 72s). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise).

hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=6, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=480, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_vn iter-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB (DATA-COVERAGE lever): train_n 200 -> 480 (~35% -> ~83% of the 579-slice train pool). BASE = iter-1 BEST config (vn_n_filters=16, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_normalize_filters=False; NOT the regressed iter-2/3/4). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, ALL BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor, baseline_PSNR 34.08): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 PSNR 32.40 RMSE 1.199e-3 (N_k=16, lam=0.0023, elapsed 1295.7s) <- BEST; iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (N_k 16->24 capacity UP -> REGRESSED -0.0133, 1351.7s); iter-3 SSIM 0.768197 PSNR 32.07 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05 DC UP -> REGRESSED -0.0238, 1159.6s); iter-4 SSIM 0.73363 PSNR 23.80 RMSE 3.228e-3 (vn_normalize_filters F->T -> REGRESSED -0.0346, 1339.8s). LIMITER / FAILURE MODE: every STRUCTURAL knob tried (capacity^, DC-weight^, filter-constraint) made it WORSE; loss flat by ep3 so it is NOT under-training; the learned VN regulariser term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i u) collapses to a BLUNT SMOOTHER that drags the recon monotonically below its own FBP init. iter-4's terminal falsifier ('SSIM<=0.84 with the regulariser constrained -> structurally FBP-bounded') FIRED. BUT one axis is UNTESTED and shared by ALL 4 iters: every iter trained on the SAME 200/579 (35%) stratified subset. MECHANISM CONFIRMED (this turn): hammernik_vn build_dataset calls load_val_split(split='train', n=train_n) = a FIXED stratified subset chosen ONCE (round-robin across ps-groups, sel=sorted(picks)), then the train loop reshuffles ONLY that subset via torch.randperm(train_n) per epoch -- it does NOT use RotatingSubsetDataset. So train_n=200 = the net only ever sees 35% of the 579-slice train pool -> train_n IS a LIVE data-coverage lever (same mechanism as uswin train_n 200->480 hr 0.3532->0.3829 and itnet_v3 200->400 hr 0.3123->0.3288). This is the strongest untried axis AND the cleanest single-knob test of whether the regulariser degradation is data-coverage-starved (200 slices too few for the 16-filter bank to learn an edge-preserving rather than smoothing regulariser) vs a true structural ceiling. HYPOTHESIS: if the degradation is data-starved, train_n 200->480 lifts val_ssim above the iter-1 0.80528 and toward/over the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER (terminal): if val_ssim stays <=0.81 (still <FBP, hr=0) even at 2.4x the training data, hammernik_vn is CONFIRMED structurally FBP-bounded on rebinned 2304-view Mayo LDCT with the data-coverage lever EXHAUSTED -> file the negative result and drive remaining iters to document the ceiling. GRAD-STEP PARITY (isolate DATA COVERAGE from extra optimization): iter-1 was max_train_s=1000-bound and ran ~7 epochs at 200 slices = ~1400 grad-slices. At train_n=480, max_train_s=1000 (kept) caps ~2.9 epochs (480x2.9 ~= 1392 grad-slices) -> near-identical optimization budget, so the comparison isolates COVERAGE not extra steps. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): iter-1 trained ~7 ep / 1000s at 200 slices => ~143 s/ep => ~0.715 s/slice/ep; at 480 slices ~343 s/ep, so max_train_s=1000 trips at ~2.9 ep (epochs=6 is just an upper bound the wall trips first). Total ~= 1000 (train wall) + ~160 (score 214 + figure) ~= 1160s, under the 1800s SLURM kill, ~640s margin. MEMORY-SAFE: identical per-step footprint to iter-1 (batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=16 within the 16 GB RTX5000; cf. hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM at 72s). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise).

BASE = iter-1 BEST config (vn_n_filters=16, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_normalize_filters=False, train_n=200; NOT the regressed iter-2/3/4 and NOT iter-5 train_n=480). Capacity (filters), DC-weight (lambda), filter-constraint, AND data-coverage (train_n) are now ALL exhausted -- each either regressed or barely moved. HYPOTHESIS: with vn_T 5->8 the extra projector-DC re-anchoring lifts val_ssim above the run-best 0.80886 toward the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER (terminal): if val_ssim stays <= 0.81 (still <FBP, hr=0) even at deeper unrolling, hammernik_vn is CONFIRMED structurally FBP-bounded on rebinned 2304-view Mayo LDCT with ALL architectural axes exhausted (capacity, DC-weight, filter-constraint, data-coverage, AND depth) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT and drive the remaining iters to DOCUMENT the ceiling toward iter-20, not chase it. BASE = iter-5 (run-BEST: vn_n_filters=16, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_normalize_filters=False, train_n=480, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_init=fbp). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, all <= ~0.84 LD-FBP floor, baseline_PSNR 34.08): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (N_k=16,lam=0.0023,vn_T=5); iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (N_k 16->24 capacity^ REGRESSED); iter-3 SSIM 0.76820 (lam 0.0023->0.05 DC^ REGRESSED); iter-4 SSIM 0.73363 (normalize_filters F->T REGRESSED); iter-5 SSIM 0.80886 (train_n 200->480 -> +0.0036 run-BEST); iter-6 SSIM 0.66729 (vn_T 5->8 depth^ -> REGRESSED HARD -0.142). Mechanism: over-applied DC steps re-inject the noisy 2304-view LD-FBP adjoint and DEGRADE the recon; fewer steps let the learned denoiser show through. The hammernik_vn analog is vn_T. CRITICAL: vn_T has only EVER been raised (5->8 at iter-6, which crashed SSIM to 0.667) or held at 5 -- NEVER LOWERED. vn_T-DOWN is the GENUINELY-UNTRIED, family-proven direction, AND iter-6 vn_T^ crashing to 0.667 is DIRECT evidence for the over-unrolling/DC-re-injection limiter (more in-loop projector DC steps = more noisy-LD-adjoint re-injection = worse). LIMITER = over-unrolling re-injecting noise (the itnet_v2 mechanism), now evidenced by iter-6. vn_T 5->2 cuts the in-loop PYRO-NN projector DC re-anchoring from 5 to 2 -> less noisy-LD-adjoint re-injection, letting the 16-filter learned regulariser/denoiser dominate.
